data.#mSetting: Room 12 – self-contained ESE classroom, specials, cafeteria, bus line
data.@m.team: Classroom teacher, two paraprofessionals, SLP, OT, assistant principal, parent
data.@m.fba: FBA in progress – records review (RR-1) and indirect assessment (IA-1) complete; descriptive data being collected on ABC-1 and SP-1
data.@m.plan: BIP due at the annual IEP meeting; this form sets the targets the plan will carry
data.@cand[3].beh: Property destruction (sweeping materials off the desk)
data.@cand[5].beh: Refusal to start work (no response for 30 s)
data.@cand[6].beh: Lining up, straightening, and closing other people’s materials (arranging and ordering)
data.@m.rationale: Seven behaviors were nominated across three informants. Prioritization weighted risk of injury first, then interference with instruction, then whether the behavior is a cusp that opens access to less restrictive settings. Five targets are carried forward: one cluster, three single topographies (one of them arranging and ordering, a higher-level restricted repetitive behavior), and one replacement behavior.
data.@clus[0].resp: Block, prompt the break mand and honor it; aggression never ends the demand
data.@clus[0].top[0].f: Hitting an adult with an open or closed hand
data.@clus[0].top[1].f: Kicking an adult below the knee
data.@clus[0].dec: Keep as cluster — all three share an escape function, the same antecedent (independent academic demand), and the same planned consequence
data.@clus[1].resp: Differs by topography — this is what broke the cluster
data.@clus[1].dec: Split into: property destruction (monitor only, tangible) and screaming (monitor only, escape). The two do not share a function or a planned response, so one label would hide the difference.
data.@tgt[0].ctx: Independent academic work in Room 12; occasionally at the bus line
data.@tgt[0].def: Forceful contact of the student’s hand, foot, or head with any part of an adult’s body — audible on contact, leaving a visible mark, or displacing the adult’s body part. Includes contact made while the adult is presenting, prompting, or withdrawing a task.
data.@tgt[0].ex:
Striking the aide’s forearm with an open hand while a worksheet is placed on the desk.
Kicking the teacher’s shin during a hand-over-hand prompt.
Dragging fingernails across an adult’s wrist as the adult reaches for the task materials.
A single light but audible slap to the adult’s shoulder when told “first work, then tablet.”
data.@tgt[0].nex:
Contact made while the adult physically guides the student as part of the agreed escort procedure.
Accidental contact when the student turns quickly and brushes an adult.
Hitting the desk, the wall, or task materials rather than a person.
Reaching toward an adult without contact.
data.@tgt[0].border: Contact through clothing counts if it is audible or displaces the body part. Contact with an adult’s hand while the student pushes materials away counts only if the hand is the point of contact rather than the materials. A strike launched from 15.24 cm (6 in.) or greater counts as forceful by distance even when it is not audible (distance threshold after Bann & Morris, 2026).
data.@tgt[0].excl: Not scored during an approved physical escort. Not scored if the adult initiates the contact.
data.@tgt[0].on: The moment any body part makes contact with the adult
data.@tgt[0].off: 10 s have passed with no further contact
data.@tgt[0].unit: Each contact = 1; a new episode is counted after 10 s without contact
data.@tgt[0].rep: Hands a break card and waits (see target 4)
data.@tgt[0].sv: Teacher and both aides rated the definition as usable without further explanation (4/4 on the classroom survey)
data.@tgt[1].ctx: Independent academic work; occasionally during dressing at home
data.@tgt[1].def: Contact of the student’s open palm with the side or top of the student’s own head, audible from 1 m away or producing visible reddening.
data.@tgt[1].ex:
Striking the right temple once with an open palm during a writing task.
Three rapid open-palm strikes to the top of the head after a demand is repeated.
An audible palm strike to the head while the student is alone at the desk.
data.@tgt[1].nex:
Resting the head in the hands.
Scratching or rubbing the scalp.
Tapping the head lightly with a fingertip, not audible and leaving no mark.
Bumping the head on a surface by accident.
data.@tgt[1].border: A closed-fist strike counts and is noted separately in the comment column. A strike to the head with an object does not count under this definition; it is recorded separately as self-injury with an object. A palm strike launched from 15.24 cm (6 in.) or greater counts by distance even when it is not audible (Bann & Morris, 2026).
data.@tgt[1].excl: Not scored during documented illness-related head holding until the nurse clears the student.
data.@tgt[1].on: The moment the palm contacts the head
data.@tgt[1].off: 5 s have passed with no further strike
data.@tgt[1].unit: Each strike = 1; a new episode is counted after 5 s without a strike
data.@tgt[1].rep: Hands a break card and waits
data.@tgt[1].sv: Parent confirmed the definition matches what is seen at home (3/4)
data.@tgt[2].def: Moving more than 2 m from the assigned area without adult permission, or crossing the classroom threshold to leave the room without permission.
data.@tgt[2].ex:
Walking out of the classroom door during independent math.
Leaving the cafeteria table and moving to the far wall without asking.
Stepping into the hallway mid-transition and continuing past the neighboring door.
data.@tgt[2].nex:
Moving to the agreed calm corner, which is inside the assigned area.
Leaving the area with adult permission, including a granted break.
Standing up beside the desk without moving away.
Walking to the bathroom on the posted schedule.
data.@tgt[2].border: A granted break to the calm corner is never elopement. If permission is requested and refused and the student leaves anyway, it counts.
data.@tgt[2].excl: Not scored during a fire drill or any evacuation.
data.@tgt[2].on: The moment the student passes 2 m from the assigned area or crosses the threshold
data.@tgt[2].off: The student has returned to the assigned area and remained for 60 s
data.@tgt[2].unit: Each departure = 1; a new episode is counted once the student has returned and remained for 60 s
data.@tgt[2].rep: Hands a break card and waits
data.@tgt[2].sv: Team agreed the 2 m criterion is workable in both rooms (4/4)
data.@tgt[3].ctx: Every independent academic demand in Room 12
data.@tgt[3].def: Picking up the break card and placing it in the adult’s open hand, or within 15 cm of the adult on the desk, within 10 s of a demand and without a physical or gestural prompt.
data.@tgt[3].ex:
Lifting the card from the desk corner and handing it to the aide when a worksheet is presented.
Placing the card on the adult’s open palm after the teacher says “time for writing.”
Sliding the card to the edge of the desk nearest the adult while looking at the adult.
data.@tgt[3].nex:
Touching the card without moving it.
Handing the card over only after the adult points at it (scored as prompted).
Saying “no” or pushing materials away without using the card.
Handing the card over more than 10 s after the demand.
data.@tgt[3].border: A card handed over during an ongoing aggression episode is still scored, and the break is honored; the aggression is recorded separately.
data.@tgt[3].excl: Not scored when no demand was presented.
data.@tgt[3].on: The card leaves the desk surface toward the adult
data.@tgt[3].off: The card is in the adult’s hand or within 15 cm of the adult
data.@tgt[3].unit: Opportunities = demand presentations; scored as independent, prompted, or absent
data.@tgt[3].sv: Teacher rated the response as easy to honor within 2 s during instruction (4/4)
data.@tgt[4].ctx: Room 12, the resource room, and transitions; reported at home
data.@tgt[4].def: RRB episode: any instance of touching or rearranging items in a disruptive manner — without permission, or not related to retrieving or putting away leisure or academic materials, or not using the item as the manufacturer intended. Onset: the student moves or attempts to move, throws away, opens, closes, or otherwise fixes or arranges an item in a way that is repetitive, disruptive to the ongoing activity, or disruptive to another person.
data.@tgt[4].ex:
Lining the markers in the caddy by color while the teacher is giving directions
Closing the teacher’s open desk drawer on the way to the carpet
Straightening peers’ chairs under the tables during independent work
Turning the trash-can lid until it sits square, repeatedly
Picking lint from a peer’s sweater
Throwing away a peer’s crumpled worksheet without asking
data.@tgt[4].nex:
Putting away the student’s own math materials at clean-up
Completing a puzzle or sorting task that was assigned
Lining up toy cars during free play when the lining is part of the play
Pushing in the student’s own chair when asked
Throwing away the student’s own trash at the end of lunch
data.@tgt[4].border: An otherwise appropriate act (putting an item in the trash) counts when it disrupts the current activity or another person. Fixing items in the student’s own cubby during clean-up is not scored.
data.@tgt[4].excl: Not scored during pretend play with leisure materials; not scored when staff requested the arrangement.
data.@tgt[4].on: First contact with the item in a fixing or arranging movement
data.@tgt[4].off: 1 s without contact with the item, or contact with a new item
data.@tgt[4].unit: Each episode = 1 and its duration is recorded; a new episode after a 1-s pause or on contact with a new item; episodes per min for the functional analysis
data.@tgt[4].rep: Engages with a competing item from the A-CSA list (see Forms EA-1 and TD-1)
data.@tgt[4].sv: Teacher and parent rated the example list as matching what they see (4/4); the parent added the drawer example
data.@rrb.family: Higher-level: arranging, ordering, rigid routines, insistence on sameness
data.@rrb.disrupt: Reported about 15 times a day; the teacher judges that it interferes with instruction because the student leaves work to fix items across the room
data.@rrb.s.note: Leaves the area to fix items in the hallway; whines and pushes the adult’s hand away when blocked; emergency physical management has never been needed
data.@rrb.measure: Frequency and duration of episodes; episodes per min for the functional analysis
data.@rrb.record: Continuous 1-s recording from video in the FA sessions; 10-s partial interval live in the classroom, with the loss of duration stated
data.@rrb.ioa: At least 33% of sessions per measure; 1-s bin agreement
data.@rrb.train: 80% agreement from the written definition before baseline
data.@rrb.eng: Engagement: any attempt to manipulate the test stimulus or an available leisure item that is not destructive or harmful; includes RRB with the item (lining up game pieces); excludes mere contact such as holding (Hagopian et al., 2020).
data.@rrb.feng: Functional item engagement: using the test stimulus or leisure item in a manner the same as or similar to the manufacturer’s intended purpose; mutually exclusive with RRB for the same item.
data.@rrb.emo: Emotional responses: whining, crying, screaming, aggression, head- or body-directed self-injury, escape attempts or physical resistance, destroying session materials (after Verriden & Roscoe, 2019).
data.@rrb.mand: Mand to end the session: “I am all done” or “I want to leave” by speech or the AAC device; a new instance after 30 s.
data.@ft.applied: Aggression (target 1) and self-injury (target 2): a strike launched from 15.24 cm (6 in.) or greater counts as forceful by distance, written into their borderline rules
data.@ft.setup: Not used: elopement is measured by the 2 m / threshold rule on the target card in the classroom, with no second room
data.@ioa[0].n: 1 of 20 intervals disagreed (a brush against the aide during a transition); the accidental-contact non-example settled it, no edit
data.@ioa[1].n: 2 of 20 intervals disagreed (light palm touches to the head); the audible-from-1-m criterion settled them, no edit
data.@ioa[3].n: 1 of 13 demands disagreed (prompted vs. independent); the 10 s window added the day before settled it, no edit
data.@ioa[4].i: 1-s bin agreement from video (frequency and duration)
data.@ioa[4].n: 3 disagreements on episode offset (the 1-s pause); the pause rule was re-trained, no edit
data.@rev[0].c: Initial definition drafted from the records review
data.@rev[1].c: Added the audible / visible-mark criterion after two disagreements
data.@rev[2].c: Changed from “leaves the room” to the 2 m / threshold rule
data.@rev[3].c: Added the 10 s window so prompted trials are scored separately

DD-1.title: Daily Target Behavior Data Sheet & Visual Analysis

data.~17: Forceful contact of the student’s hand, foot, or head with any part of an adult’s body — audible on contact, leaving a visible mark, or displacing the adult’s body part. Includes contact made while the adult is presenting, prompting, or withdrawing a task.
data.~28: Contact of the student’s open palm with the side or top of the student’s own head, audible from 1 m away or producing visible reddening.
data.~39: Moving more than 2 m from the assigned area without adult permission, or crossing the classroom threshold to leave the room without permission.
data.~50: RRB episode: any instance of touching or rearranging items in a disruptive manner — without permission, or not related to retrieving or putting away leisure or academic materials, or not using the item as the manufacturer intended. Onset: the student moves or attempts to move, throws away, opens, closes, or otherwise fixes or arranges an item in a way that is repetitive, disruptive to the ongoing activity, or disruptive to another person.
data.~54: Hands a break card and waits (see target 4)
data.~65: Hands a break card and waits
data.~76: Hands a break card and waits
data.~87: Engages with a competing item from the A-CSA list (see Forms EA-1 and TD-1)
data.~105: Picking up the break card and placing it in the adult’s open hand, or within 15 cm of the adult on the desk, within 10 s of a demand and without a physical or gestural prompt.

behaviors.label: Aggression
behaviors.def: Forceful contact of the student’s hand, foot, or head with any part of an adult’s body — audible on contact, leaving a visible mark, or displacing the adult’s body part. Includes contact made while the adult is presenting, prompting, or withdrawing a task.
behaviors.ex:
Striking the aide’s forearm with an open hand while a worksheet is placed on the desk.
Kicking the teacher’s shin during a hand-over-hand prompt.
Dragging fingernails across an adult’s wrist as the adult reaches for the task materials.
A single light but audible slap to the adult’s shoulder when told “first work, then tablet.”
behaviors.nex:
Contact made while the adult physically guides the student as part of the agreed escort procedure.
Accidental contact when the student turns quickly and brushes an adult.
Hitting the desk, the wall, or task materials rather than a person.
Reaching toward an adult without contact.
behaviors.unit: Each contact = 1; a new episode is counted after 10 s without contact
behaviors.rep: Hands a break card and waits (see target 4)
behaviors.ctx: Independent academic work in Room 12; occasionally at the bus line
behaviors.excl: Not scored during an approved physical escort. Not scored if the adult initiates the contact.

behaviors.label: Self-injury – head hitting
behaviors.def: Contact of the student’s open palm with the side or top of the student’s own head, audible from 1 m away or producing visible reddening.
behaviors.ex:
Striking the right temple once with an open palm during a writing task.
Three rapid open-palm strikes to the top of the head after a demand is repeated.
An audible palm strike to the head while the student is alone at the desk.
behaviors.nex:
Resting the head in the hands.
Scratching or rubbing the scalp.
Tapping the head lightly with a fingertip, not audible and leaving no mark.
Bumping the head on a surface by accident.
behaviors.unit: Each strike = 1; a new episode is counted after 5 s without a strike
behaviors.rep: Hands a break card and waits
behaviors.ctx: Independent academic work; occasionally during dressing at home
behaviors.excl: Not scored during documented illness-related head holding until the nurse clears the student.

behaviors.label: Elopement
behaviors.def: Moving more than 2 m from the assigned area without adult permission, or crossing the classroom threshold to leave the room without permission.
behaviors.ex:
Walking out of the classroom door during independent math.
Leaving the cafeteria table and moving to the far wall without asking.
Stepping into the hallway mid-transition and continuing past the neighboring door.
behaviors.nex:
Moving to the agreed calm corner, which is inside the assigned area.
Leaving the area with adult permission, including a granted break.
Standing up beside the desk without moving away.
Walking to the bathroom on the posted schedule.
behaviors.unit: Each departure = 1; a new episode is counted once the student has returned and remained for 60 s
behaviors.rep: Hands a break card and waits
behaviors.excl: Not scored during a fire drill or any evacuation.

behaviors.label: Break request (replacement)
behaviors.def: Picking up the break card and placing it in the adult’s open hand, or within 15 cm of the adult on the desk, within 10 s of a demand and without a physical or gestural prompt.
behaviors.ex:
Lifting the card from the desk corner and handing it to the aide when a worksheet is presented.
Placing the card on the adult’s open palm after the teacher says “time for writing.”
Sliding the card to the edge of the desk nearest the adult while looking at the adult.
behaviors.nex:
Touching the card without moving it.
Handing the card over only after the adult points at it (scored as prompted).
Saying “no” or pushing materials away without using the card.
Handing the card over more than 10 s after the demand.
behaviors.unit: Opportunities = demand presentations; scored as independent, prompted, or absent
behaviors.ctx: Every independent academic demand in Room 12
behaviors.excl: Not scored when no demand was presented.

behaviors.label: Arranging and ordering (higher-level RRB)
behaviors.def: RRB episode: any instance of touching or rearranging items in a disruptive manner — without permission, or not related to retrieving or putting away leisure or academic materials, or not using the item as the manufacturer intended. Onset: the student moves or attempts to move, throws away, opens, closes, or otherwise fixes or arranges an item in a way that is repetitive, disruptive to the ongoing activity, or disruptive to another person.
behaviors.ex:
Lining the markers in the caddy by color while the teacher is giving directions
Closing the teacher’s open desk drawer on the way to the carpet
Straightening peers’ chairs under the tables during independent work
Turning the trash-can lid until it sits square, repeatedly
Picking lint from a peer’s sweater
Throwing away a peer’s crumpled worksheet without asking
behaviors.nex:
Putting away the student’s own math materials at clean-up
Completing a puzzle or sorting task that was assigned
Lining up toy cars during free play when the lining is part of the play
Pushing in the student’s own chair when asked
Throwing away the student’s own trash at the end of lunch
behaviors.unit: Each episode = 1 and its duration is recorded; a new episode after a 1-s pause or on contact with a new item; episodes per min for the functional analysis
behaviors.rep: Engages with a competing item from the A-CSA list (see Forms EA-1 and TD-1)
behaviors.ctx: Room 12, the resource room, and transitions; reported at home
behaviors.excl: Not scored during pretend play with leisure materials; not scored when staff requested the arrangement.
